newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Chinese Estates to spin off China unit.
newsitem.headline: Chinese Estates to spin off China unit.

text.p: Chinese Estates Holdings Ltd said in a statement on Monday it proposed to spin off its property development and investment businesses in China under a new holding company named Evergo China Holdings Ltd.

Under the proposal, Chinese Estates will distribute to its shareholders 25 percent of the 1.2 billion Evergo China shares in issue and to be issued in the form of a speical interim dividend in specie.
Dividends will be paid in the proportion of 623 Evergo China shares for every 4,000 shares of Chinese Estates held.
But no Evergo China shares will be distributed to the company's overseas shareholders, the statement said.

Chinese Estates' majority shareholder Joseph Lau, who currently holds 1,048 million Chinese Estates shares, or 54.44 percent of the company's issued share capital, will privately place about 163 milion Evergo China shares, or 13.5 percent of its issued shares, representing his entitlement to the special interim dividend in specie.
At least 25 percent of the issued shares of Evergo China will be in public hands on completion of the placement.
Evergo China is to focus on developing and investing in properties in major or emerging Chinese cities.
Its property projects, mainly in Beijing, Shanghai and southern China's Guangdong province, have been independently valued at HK$2.36 billion as at July 31, 1996.

Application for a separate listing of Evergo China has been submitted to the Stock Exchange. Trading of its shares is expected to start by November 20 should its application be successful, the statement said.
After the listing Evergo China will remain a subsidiary of Chinese Estates. Joseph Lau and Thomas Lau, both directors of Chinese Estates, will also be directors of Evergo China.
